tracking_failures.kind: shuttle tracker parked on an undetected fixed object
tracking_failures.notes: TrackNet rests on a mark on the back wall at about (400, 175) in four stretches of 11-15 frames: 4170-4180, 7216-7228, 7247-7261, 7347-7360. The fixed-point detector found only the large parked point at (918, 222), which holds 2340 frames; this one holds 59 across four runs and falls under the threshold. The labelled contacts at 7227 and 7248 sit inside two of these stretches, the far player is untracked from 7228 to 7248, and the current pipeline emits no hit at either frame. That is consistent with both being detector artefacts the candidate-verdict migration confirmed, but it is not proof, so neither label was changed.

migrated_from.note: Discarded rows recorded that a particular candidate was not a hit, which is true of a configuration rather than of the video. The matcher re-derives false positives for whatever configuration is scored.

label_revisions.what: Every rally end and rally 1's start re-measured from the working video at 8-frame granularity.
label_revisions.why: Rally 2's labelled end of 1098 was 2.7 seconds into dead time. Checking it exposed a systematic bias: five of six ends were labelled 20 to 40 frames after play stopped, and rally 2 by 160. The convention is now that a rally ends when the shuttle lands or the point is otherwise decided, not when the players finish walking.
label_revisions.method: Frames pulled from outputs/test-video2/work.mp4 with ffmpeg and read directly. Each end was bracketed by one frame with the point visibly live and one with both players upright and disengaged, then set between them.
label_revisions.effect: The correction was applied to all six ends before any of them was scored, and it moves two ends earlier than the detector reports and four later. Rally 4's correction made a rest-based end rule fail that the uncorrected label had passed. Rally starts were also aligned to the labelled serve contact, moving three of them 11 to 14 frames earlier. That works against the detector, whose starts already ran late.

label_revisions.what: Removed one of two byte-identical contact rows at frame 2006 (hitter far, no notes).
label_revisions.why: A racket cannot strike the shuttle twice in the same frame, so one row was a data-entry duplicate. It was unmatchable by construction -- each contact is claimed once, so at most one prediction could ever pair with the two of them -- which made it a permanent false negative that no detector change could clear. The hitters around it read near, near, near, far, far, near, far with both rows and alternate correctly with one.
label_revisions.method: Found by checking the interval between consecutive labelled contacts while validating the 0.30s consolidation window: the closest pair in the file was 0.000s apart. The rows are identical in every field.
label_revisions.effect: Labelled contacts fall from 62 to 61 and rally shots from 60 to 59. No accuracy figure moves: precision, recall, F1, hitter accuracy and every rally number are unchanged. The duplicate was harmless only by luck -- match_contacts tracks claimed contacts by frame number, so the two rows collapsed to one entry and a prediction did match frame 2006. Had nothing matched it, both rows would have been counted as missed and the file would have carried a false negative no detector change could ever clear. score_clip now refuses a truth file containing two contacts on one frame, so this cannot come back silently.

label_revisions.what: Hitter corrected on four contacts: 870 far, 2689 far, 4510 far, 5060 near.
label_revisions.why: Raised unprompted by the project owner while labelling shot types. The previews stated the hitter this file held, and on these four the owner said it was the other player. Each correction also removes an impossible sequence: a singles rally alternates, and every one of the four sat in a run where one player was credited with two contacts in a row. Two independent reasons agreeing is why these were applied and the remaining violations were not.
label_revisions.method: Applied by frame to outputs/test-video2/truth.json. No detector, model or threshold was consulted. The alternation check (badminton_poc.truth.find_impossible_alternations) was run before and after: 13 impossible pairs before, 6 after.
label_revisions.effect: 6 impossible pairs remain and are NOT fixed here, because the rule says the labelling is wrong somewhere in each pair without saying which contact is wrong, and some are likely to be real contacts nobody recorded rather than wrong hitters. They are listed in every evaluation under label_consistency until a human resolves them.
label_revisions.context: This clip's contacts were migrated from candidate verdicts, and its true_hitter agreed with detected_hitter on 60 of 61 real hits -- the signature of a pass that read the detector's answer and confirmed it. Clips 3 and 5 were re-labelled blind and carry zero impossible pairs; clip 2 carried thirteen. It has not had that treatment.

label_revisions.what: Hitter at 1877 corrected near -> far; contacts added at 4017 (near) and 4316 (near).
label_revisions.why: Four of clip 2's six impossible alternations were resolvable from evidence already on disk. Two were one error: the run 1801/1877/1931 is three contacts credited to near, and 1877 is the wrong one. The other two were gaps of 1.9 and 1.8 seconds hiding a real contact each.
label_revisions.method: Shuttle trajectory from tracknet/work_ball.csv for the reversals, wrist keypoints from players.jsonl for the swing apex, and video frames read directly for confirmation. Each conclusion was checked against a frame before being applied.
label_revisions.provenance: DERIVED BY A MODEL, not by the project owner. Every contact touched here carries hitter_source=model-derived-2026-09-16 so it can be found and reverted, and neither added contact is given a shot type, because naming the stroke is the owner's call and Milestone 2 skips a contact that has none. Clips 3 and 5 remain entirely hand-labelled; this makes clip 2 a mixed labelling and that must be stated wherever it is scored.
